subject: Information Theory
title: Zero Entropy
description: Learn Zero Entropy in one minute.

hook.text: A source that always outputs the same symbol has zero entropy. You already know every future message.

buildup.text: Zero entropy means zero surprise, zero uncertainty, zero information per symbol.

discovery.text: Mathematically: if P(x)=1, then -1×log₂(1)=0. The log of 1 is always zero.

twist.text: A channel carrying a constant signal wastes its capacity entirely. It transmits bits but communicates nothing.

climax.text: Zero entropy is perfect predictability. Useful for structure, useless for communicating new things.

punchline.text: No surprise, no information, zero entropy.

quiz.question: When does a source have zero entropy?
options: When all outcomes are equally likely
